title: The divers who forgot on land

probes.question: Where did divers best recall words they had learned under water?
True or false: changing the context between learning and recall reduced the divers' ability to recall words.

image.alt: Two scuba divers explore a coral-covered shipwreck underwater, one holding a red light.

panels.text: Researchers noticed that deep-sea divers remembered less about events they had seen underwater once they had resurfaced.
In 1975, Godden and Baddeley tested whether the setting mattered. Divers learned word lists in two places: under water and on dry land.
Words learned under water were recalled better under water, and words learned on land were recalled better on land.
Changing the context between learning and recall made it harder to remember the words. The study likely started today's research on context-dependent memory.
